item.title: You're Invited: Eastland Plan Kickoff
item.description:
Eastland Community Plan Kickoff 

The Eastland Community Plan is getting started and we need your voice to make this plan a success.

Date: Saturday, October 14th, 2023 

Time: 11:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. 

Location: Barnett Community Center, 1184 Barnett Road, Columbus, OH 43227 

Join us to kick off the Eastland Community Plan on October 14th. Now is the time to envision a new future for the Eastland area, one that is equitable and prosperous for everyone. We need your voice and your ideas to make that happen. Be part of the planning process to create the roadmap for the future of your community.  

This meeting will include: 

  • Updates from City of Columbus leadership on ongoing projects and initiatives that impact the Eastland area; 
  • A brief presentation about the Eastland Community Plan process; 
  • Engaging activities to understand how you experience the Eastland area; and  
  • Kid-friendly activities so the whole family can attend and participate. 

Lunch will also be provided. Please register to attend the meeting using the link below so we can plan accordingly, as space is limited. We hope to see you there! 

Click here to Register!

item.title: Help us Keep Columbus Beautiful!
item.description:
The Department of Public Service and our Keep Columbus Beautiful program are gearing up for another litter cleanup event this month, and department employee teams are forming now. During our cleanup last spring, hundreds of you volunteered time and collected nearly 4,500 pounds — more than 2 tons — of litter along Columbus streets.

Our fall cleanup is set for Friday, Oct. 20. Public Service coworkers are encouraged to create teams and select a team captain to register team members. Teams may choose to perform their cleanup from 9 to 11 a.m. or from 1 to 3 p.m., or you may find another approved time on Oct. 20 that works best for your team.

Please check with your supervisor to see if you can participate in the cleanup as part of your regular workday activities. For more information, email keepcolumbusbeautiful@columbus.gov. Keep Columbus Beautiful will deliver cleanup supplies to a convenient location to make it easy for your team to get started.

The department’s employee litter cleanup events are an enjoyable way to work together to keep Columbus beautiful and prevent litter from making its way into city storm drains and polluting our waterways.

Thank you for your volunteerism and commitment to our community!

item.title: 2024 NALA Application is Now Open
item.description:
2024 NALA Application is Now Open!

 

Apply for the New American Leadership Academy 

We are pleased to share with you that the application for the 2024 New American Leadership Academy (NALA) cohort is now available.

NALA is an opportunity for New American professionals to foster their personal development by building knowledge in civic engagement, and discovering new ways to contribute to their respective communities and the city of Columbus at large.  Academy participants receive mentorship and professional development on topics including government, civic engagement, and strategic collaboration along with  implicit bias training, public speaking, and conflict resolution and management. The bi-monthly sessions will begin in March 2024 and end in November 2024.

Applications will be accepted now through November 17, 2023. For more information, and to apply online, please visit www.columbus.gov/nala.

item.title: Opportunity City: Welcome to Fall, Columbus!
item.description:
Happy Fall, Columbus!

As I reflect on a fantastic summer, I am grateful for all of the great activities our city had to offer, including packed festivals, concerts at the Columbus Commons and, perhaps most notably, over $20 million in direct support for summer youth programming. But the arrival of fall does not mean the fun is over. I look forward to our final Rise Up! CBUS in the Hilltop tomorrow, Sept. 28, and CelebrateOne’s First Birthday Party on Saturday, Oct. 7 – with many more exciting events coming down the pike. Be sure to follow my Facebook, Instagram and X accounts for regular updates on opportunities to stay connected and involved across the community.

Sincerely,

Mayor Andy Ginther

Summer programming keeps youth safe

Summer camps and programs serve as safe, constructive outlets for youth to learn, grow and develop. This summer, the City of Columbus devoted $20.1 million toward keeping teens and kids engaged, preparing them for future careers, and helping them to get outside and play— all while keeping their minds sharp in preparation for the new school year. According to the latest count, our summer programming reached over 15,000 participants.

Summer programs are also a reliable way to connect kids with nutritious meals. I am proud to share that our Go Lunch! program served over 240,800 meals.

We have an obligation to invest in every person who calls Columbus home – particularly our young people. And we owe it to our future leaders to provide them with the skills and knowledge they need to lay the groundwork for a lifetime of success.

New affordable apartments replace abandoned music venue

Last week, I celebrated the opening of The Sinclair apartments with the Columbus Metropolitan Housing Authority, NRP Group, the Ohio Housing Financing Agency, Huntington National Bank and State Senator Hearcel Craig. These 180 high-quality, affordable apartments mark a major milestone in my Columbus Housing Strategy, our blueprint for building the housing we need while including everyone in our region’s prosperity.

At the end of the day, no resident should have to spend more than 30 percent of their income to live in safe housing in a neighborhood of their choice. And a family earning $50,000 a year should be able to choose where their family lives. By working with our partners across the region, I’m confident we’ll make this aspiration a reality for our city.

Congratulations to our rising stars in the Division of Fire

I applaud the 47 Columbus Division of Fire graduates for stepping up and committing themselves to one of our city’s most essential, dynamic and respected professions. I also commend our 3rd Fire Cadet Class, a program I started with former Fire Chief and Public Safety Director Ned Pettus to increase diversity so that our firefighters better reflect the communities they serve.

We also welcome K9 firefighter teams Jeremy Thoma and Labrador, Harry; and State Fire Marshal Jeff Koehn and Labrador, Harley. These teams will join the arson detection division, specializing in detecting 10 different liquids commonly used to start arson fires.

item.title: CelebrateOne September Newsletter
item.description:
News from CelebrateONE Columbus • September 2023

CelebrateOne Hosting

First Birthday Party October 7

We’re throwing a first birthday party!

Celebrate One is inviting all families with a baby celebrating their first birthday in 2023 to join us from 1-4 p.m. on October 7 at Columbus Commons for an outdoor celebration.  

The festivities will include music, free food, costumed characters, carnival games, early childhood education resources and a special gift from CelebrateOne for registered families. Registration is available here: https://tinyurl.com/First-Birthday-2023

CelebrateOne, created in 2014 to reduce the infant mortality rate in Franklin County, connects pregnant women and families with resources and support to ensure a healthy start to life.

“The purpose of the CelebrateOne First Birthday Party is to celebrate the monumental event of babies in our community reaching their first birthday and to connect parents with early childhood education resources so that their toddlers can thrive,” said Danielle Tong, executive director of CelebrateOne.

In 2022, approximately 17,400 babies were born in Franklin County and a total of 137 babies died before their first birthday. “We have specific Columbus neighborhoods which continue to experience unacceptably high rates of infant mortality,* with rates being disproportionately higher among Black infants,” Tong said.

*Infant mortality is the death of an infant before his or her first birthday.

Volunteers Needed at

October 7 First Birthday Party

We are busy preparing for our 2023 First Birthday Party. But we sure could use a few volunteers to help us at the October 7 event. 

Volunteers are needed to help with set up, tear down, registration and diaper bag distribution.

If you have a few hours to spare October 7, we would greatly appreciate your assistance. Sign up to volunteer here: https://signup.com/go/thKpmVC

Next Lactation Education

Class Set for September 28

Are you a new mom? One of the decisions you’ll make as a parent is how to feed your baby. Breastfeeding is a great option and has many health benefits for mom and baby. 

Benefits for Baby:

  • Naturally soothes your baby
  • Has the right amount of nutrition to help your baby grow
  • Decreases the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS)

 Benefits for Mom:

  • Helps with recovery after childbirth
  • Creates a unique bonding experience with your baby
  • Can help prevent postpartum depression and can reduce the risk of  getting certain cancers and diabetes

Want to learn more? CelebrateOne is now offering FREE in-person lactation classes with certified diversity lactation instructors.

In this class you will learn:

  • Benefits of Breastfeeding
  • Preparing for the Journey
  • Educating Your Support Team
  • Hunger Cues
  • Position and Latch
  • Common Concerns
  • Returning to Work/Breastfeeding Rights
  • Proper Storage
  • Resources and Education

Our next lactation education class is set for 1p.m. on September 28 and it will be held at our city office building, 1111 E. Broad St.

Register Here

September Marks Infant

Mortality Awareness Month

September marks Infant Mortality Awareness Month. Why is it important to know about infant mortality?

The infant mortality rate measures the number of infant deaths for every 1,000 live births. In addition to giving us key information about maternal and infant health, the infant mortality rate is an important marker of the overall health of a community. It paints a picture about general living conditions, social well-being, rates of illness, quality and access to medical care, public health practices and quality of the environment.  

In 2021, the infant mortality rate in Franklin County was 8.1 deaths per 1,000 live births compared to 5.4 in the United States that same year. The county has set a goal of five infant deaths per 1,000 live births by 2030.

When taking a look at infant mortality by race, Black babies are more than two times more likely to die than white babies. There are many factors that can cause a baby to die, including prematurity - the top cause of infant death in Franklin County (20% of infant deaths in 2022), congenital anomalies (15%), sudden infant death syndrome (13%) and infections (15%).

As we wind down Infant Mortality Awareness Month, ask yourself ‘What can I do to make the lives of birthing families safer?’ We have some ideas: Take a safe sleep ambassador training class through Columbus Public Health or direct a family to StepOne to get access to prenatal care. The most important thing anyone can do is listen to families. Let us all listen intently when they share their experiences. And then, it’s up to us to take action, because when we do more babies in Franklin County will be celebrating their first birthdays.  

CelebrateOne Announces

Two Promotions

CelebrateOne is pleased to announce the promotions of Melinda Cunningham and Kadijah Torian.

Melinda Cunningham has been appointed to the position of deputy director of the organization. She has served as CelebrateOne’s fiscal manager since 2022.

Cunningham will continue to oversee all financial matters. In her new role, she will also lead staff development and coordinate staff policies and procedures.

 

Kadijah Torian has been promoted to Senior Manager of Pregnancy and Perinatal Supports and will oversee the eight care coordinators serving in the areas of prenatal and perinatal care. Torian was previously the Assistant Manager of the Prenatal Care team.

She joined the organization in 2019 as a certified birth doula and community health worker. She has earned her certification as a diverse lactation instructor. 

“I’m excited that I get to continue to serve and support a team that is passionate about meeting our family’s most imperative needs," Torian said. "I want to hear what families and partners need from us and collaborate with them to make positive and equitable impacts. My ultimate goal is to develop a team that is not only skilled in assisting community members and stakeholders but are confident and empowered in driving forward improvements in maternal and infant health.”

222 Pregnancy Test Kits

Picked up from Libraries

A total of 222 home pregnancy test kits were picked up between June – August at the Columbus Metropolitan Main Library and 16 library branches.

Three sites, Linden, Northside and Driving Park, had the most requests for the pregnancy test kits since launching the program, in partnership with the Columbus Metropolitan Library, on June 5. A kit includes two pregnancy tests. 

“By providing the kits for free and making them easily accessible, we want people to learn as soon as possible when they are pregnant so they can get proper prenatal care," said Danielle Tong, executive director, CelebrateOne.

One out of every three moms-to-be gets prenatal care late (second trimester) or not at all. As a result, babies born too small and too early are some of the reasons infants in Franklin County die before their first birthday.

It's easy to get a pregnancy test kit, just see a library staff member. To learn more: https://new.columbus.gov/files/sharedassets/city/v/2/celebrateone/co-pregnancy-test-kit_1080-x-1080-v4-libraries-listed.jpg

Peer Education Program Accepting Applications for the 2023-2024 Academic Year

The Ohio Center for Sex Education is accepting applications for its 2023-2024 Peer Education Program.

Peer educators are teens ages 14-19 who serve as leaders and role models in the community. The peer educators promote smart decisions about reproductive health during every day conversations with their network of friends and acquaintances.  

Through this program, teens build leadership, communication and public speaking skills and also earn $500.

During the 2022-2023 academic year, 27 teens completed 20 hours of virtual training to receive the title of peer educator. By the end of the year, the teens reached 6,590 peers through in-person and online outreach events.

item.title: Councilmember Nick Bankston Sponsors Citywide Sickle Cell Awareness Month Blood Drives
item.description:
Councilmember Nick Bankston Sponsors Citywide Sickle Cell Awareness Month Blood Drives

September 7, 2023

Good afternoon City Staff,

In honor of Sickle Cell Awareness Month, Councilmember Nicholas J. Bankston has partnered with the American Red Cross to host a series of blood drives for the month of September. 

Sickle Cell Disease is an inherited blood disease that occurs in about one of every 365 Black American Births in the U.S.  It also affects people of Hispanic, Mediterranean, and South Asian descent worldwide. Four American Red Cross Blood Drives have been scheduled in support of and commitment to our own and the community. For employees' convenience, two internal employee-only drives have been scheduled in the 77 Building and Columbus Public Health, but employees are welcome to attend any drive. If you would like to register for one of the blood drives below, go to https://www.redcrossblood.org/give.html/find-drive and enter in the sponsor code assigned to your desired blood drive.

  • September 11th (Community Blood Drive) @ Central Ohio Area Agency on Aging (COAAA)
    • 3776 S High St., Columbus, OH 43207, 9:00am – 3:00pm
    • Sponsor code: COAAA
  • *September 14th (Community Blood Drive) @ American Red Cross 
    • 995 E. Broad St, 2nd floor, 10:00am-4:00pm 
    • Sponsor code: ARCCommunity
  • September 21st in the Lower Level of 77 Building
    • 77 North Front Street, 9:00am-3:00pm
    • Sponsor code: colcityhall

  • September 25th @ Columbus Public Health
    • 240 Parsons Ave., 10:00am – 4:00pm
    • Sponsor code: CPH

If you have questions about the drives, please contact Tina DeFluiter at TLDefluiter@columbus.gov. To learn more about Sickle Cell Disease, click here.

Additionally, on Monday, September 18, 2023 from 8pm to approximately 8:45pm Councilmember Bankston will host the Annual Sickle Cell Disease Awards & Illumination Ceremony after the City Council Meeting. All are welcome to attend. We look forward to seeing you and appreciate the work you all do!

item.title: Cops and Cookies 5k- Help support the Columbus Police Honor Guard
item.description:
The Columbus Division of Police Honor Guard is hosting our 11th Annual Memorial 5K and 1 Mile Kids Fun Run- now called the Cops and Cookies 5K- on Saturday, September 30th at 9:00 a.m.

The run/ walk will begin at our Police Memorial in Genoa Park.  Bring the family and come early to meet the K9 unit, SWAT team, Dive team, Therapy Dogs, the Mounted Unit, sit in a police cruiser, see the helicopter, and more!

This year, not only will there be cookies at the finish line (including MCL Bakery, Resch’s Bakery, Cheryl’s Cookies, and Crumbl Cookies) but there will be cookies at all water stops.

item.title: 5th Annual Gift of Music | August 26 – September 3, 2023
item.description:
This summer we are partnering with the Columbus Music Commission to help promote the 5th annual Gift of Music student instrument drive and encourage everyone we know to come together and support this movement!

 The Gift of Music is a Music Columbus initiative that collects gently used musical instruments and accessories for local City and Charter school students. The campaign ensures students’ access to music education and early childhood development. No instrument? No problem! You can make a donation to help purchase new ones. Just visit www.giftofmusic.info (or here: Gift of Music Go Fund Me) 

The collection dates span from August 26th to September 3rd. Donations can be made by visiting one of the drop-off locations around central Ohio, which can be found HERE (www.giftofmusic.info) !

 

For questions, contact Jennie Hanna at JNHanna@columbus.gov
